description: A set operation's ORDER BY resolves against the COMBINED OUTPUT only - measured cell by cell on a real account. An output column name works, whether it is the first branch's alias or the produced name of an un-aliased item; so does a positional ordinal, and so does an expression built over those output names. Everything else is rejected as 'invalid identifier': a SECOND branch's column name, a branch table's qualifier, a first-branch column that was NOT selected, an aliased item's PRE-ALIAS expression text (the alias REPLACES it as the output name), and any unknown name. There is no fall-through to any branch's FROM scope. Converted 1:1 from query/SetOperationOrderByTest (now retired); the Java joined the first column of each row with a pipe, so the converted steps pin the ordered row set instead.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE t1 (a INTEGER, c INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE t2 (b INTEGER, c INTEGER)
SELECT a FROM t1 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM t2 ORDER BY a
SELECT a FROM t1 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM t2 ORDER BY 1 DESC
SELECT a FROM t1 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM t2 ORDER BY a + 1
SELECT a AS x FROM t1 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM t2 ORDER BY x
CREATE TABLE t1 (a INTEGER, c INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE t2 (b INTEGER, c INTEGER)
SELECT a FROM t1 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM t2 ORDER BY b
SELECT a FROM t1 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM t2 ORDER BY t1.a
SELECT a FROM t1 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM t2 ORDER BY nosuch
SELECT a FROM t1 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM t2 ORDER BY c
SELECT a AS x FROM t1 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM t2 ORDER BY a
